latin: Ideo in anima apparet incompossibilitas contradictoriorum, quia est prima quantitas, ponens partem extra partem.
translation: The incompossibility of contradictories therefore appears in the soul, because it is the first quantity, positing part outside part.
translation_note: "ponens partem extra partem" renders the standard definition of quantity as an ordered plurality of parts external to one another; "incompossibilitas" is kept as the technical term for the incapacity of two things to hold together.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch13, from Latin at farmer1998:20462
doctrine: The thesis explains why contradictories cannot coincide in the soul as, on the preceding theses of this run, they can in a purely intellectual nature: the soul is itself "the first quantity", positing part outside part, and this quantitative extension produces the incompossibility of contradictories within it (farmer1998:20462). Farmer's note treats 3>13-18 as a single unit and refers the reader to his discussion of this part of Pico's metaphysics for traditional logic (farmer1998:20526).
context: 3>18 closes the run begun at 3>13 on whether contradictories can coincide, following 3>17's claim that in the intellect "this and that" are present without "this" being outside "that" (farmer1998:20459). Farmer connects the run to 2.31, from Thomas Aquinas, on the real distinction of essence and existence in every created thing (farmer1998:11760; farmer1998:20526).
historiography: As with 3>16, the only located scholarly mention is a footnote in the German study Erkenntnistheorie und christliche Kabbalah, which lists 3>18 alongside 3>15 and 3>16 without separate comment (kabbalah_paradigma:1705).
not_established: Whether the German study's footnote discusses 3>18's specific content beyond citing its number: not established by the excerpt consulted (kabbalah_paradigma:1705).
